page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.4xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. The host utilizes an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, backed by 40 MB of L3 cache. System memory comprises 120.0 GB of RAM, providing 7.5 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by two NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPUs delivering a combined total of 32 GB of VRAM. Bundled local storage includes a 944 GB SSD, and network throughput is provisioned with a 5 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark measurements reflect the generational characteristics of the Broadwell architecture and dual-GPU host configuration. Single-core execution demonstrates lower relative output, with stress-ng single-core scoring 954.09 and single-threaded gzip compression processing 21.45 GB/sec. When parallelized across all 16 vCPUs, multi-core operations achieve middle-tier results, reaching 9532.02 on stress-ng and 59.76 GB/sec on multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory subsystems sustain 56.56 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 31.42 GB/sec in write operations. Under application-level throughput tests, the system delivered 10.88 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 9.91 GB/sec in static web serving.

The primary operational tradeoff lies in the older CPU core architecture and lack of AVX-512 support, offset by substantial aggregate GPU compute capacity, high RAM density, and bundled high-capacity local SSD storage. Workloads that depend heavily on single-thread CPU performance may experience bottlenecks. However, applications requiring dual-GPU acceleration, moderate network transfers, and fast local scratch storage operate efficiently on this instance profile.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.4xlarge is suited for legacy deep learning training and inference pipelines, GPU-accelerated scientific simulations, computer vision preprocessing, and video rendering workloads that utilize NVIDIA CUDA libraries targeting Pascal architecture hardware.

Running on KVM virtualization, it features an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores at 2.5 GHz, supported by 120.0 GB of system memory. Compute acceleration is provided by two NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPUs offering 32 GB of total VRAM, supplemented by 944 GB of integrated local SSD storage and a 5 Gbps network interface. Benchmark results indicate modest single-thread capabilities alongside balanced multi-core throughput, recording 9532.02 points in multi-threaded stress-ng and 10.88 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory bandwidth registers 56.56 GB/sec for large uncached reads. The combination of dual discrete accelerators, ample system memory, and direct local solid-state storage makes this server instance practical for legacy machine learning model training, video transcoding, and GPU-driven scientific computing workloads.
